topIssues.title: op-core: replace the FastLZ and Fjord L1-cost fuzzers with pinned fixtures
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
The FastLZ and Fjord L1-cost fuzzers have not run in CI since #21639, not even their seeds. Proposal: replace them with fixtures that run in the normal Go test job, so every branch of the two functions is covered on each PR.

## Current state

The fuzzers compare `op-core/fees` with the Solidity and C implementations:

- `FuzzFjordCostFunction`: `L1CostFjord` against the `GasPriceOracle` predeploy
- `FuzzFastLzSolidity`: `FlzCompressLen` against Solady's LibZip
- `FuzzFastLzCgo`: `FlzCompressLen` against the C FastLZ library

All are in [`op-core/fees/fuzz/fuzz_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/849608d846/op-core/fees/fuzz/fuzz_test.go#L1) since #23864, behind the `cgo_test` build tag.

#21639 retired the Go fuzz jobs because the seed cases "run in the normal unit-test jobs". That does not hold here: the Go test jobs build with [`-tags="ci"`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/justfile#L387), so nothing compiles a `cgo_test` file. Today the fuzzers run only through a manual `just fuzz-op-core-fees`.

Their seeds are also weak. All are real Base transactions between roughly 100 bytes and 1.2 KB, and a coverage run shows they never reach:

- the 100-byte floor of the Fjord size estimate ([`fees.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/op-core/fees/fees.go#L154))
- inputs under 13 bytes, including the empty input ([`fastlz.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/op-core/fees/fastlz.go#L45))
- a hash-table hit further back than 8191 bytes, which must not count as a match ([`fastlz.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/op-core/fees/fastlz.go#L61)); no seed is long enough

## What already runs in CI

- Go: [`TestFlzCompressLen`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/op-core/fees/fastlz_test.go#L17) pins compressed lengths; [`TestFjordL1CostFuncMinimumBounds` and `TestFjordL1CostSolidityParity`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/op-core/fees/fees_test.go#L67-L101) pin the cost function, including the floor.
- Rust: [`op-revm/src/fast_lz.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/rust/op-revm/src/fast_lz.rs#L113-L145) pins compressed lengths and compares its implementation with LibZip executed in revm, on the same Base transactions.

Neither `FlzCompressLen` table has a fixture for a far hash-table hit, and the Go table has none for a non-empty input under 13 bytes.

## Proposal

1. Add fixtures for the uncovered branches to `TestFlzCompressLen`:
   - a few inputs under 13 bytes
   - an incompressible block longer than 32 bytes (literal-run encoding)
   - a match longer than 262 bytes with a remainder on each side of the 2-byte/3-byte boundary
   - a sequence that repeats more than 8191 bytes apart
   - a hash collision that is not a match
2. Take the expected values from the references once: add the fixtures as fuzz seeds, run the three targets locally, then pin the results.
3. Assert the same new vectors in `op-revm`'s `test_flz_compress_len`, as the [cross-implementation parity rule](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c5b8a82f664da7ad05111c3307d3c95575e82da2/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md#cross-implementation-parity) asks.
4. Add an end-to-end Fjord fee vector from transaction bytes to fee, below and above the floor.
5. Keep the vendored C FastLZ as an oracle: turn `FuzzFastLzCgo` into a table test that compares `FlzCompressLen` with the C library over the same fixtures, without the `cgo_test` tag, so the normal Go test job runs it. C FastLZ is the original implementation; LibZip and the Go and Rust code are ports of it. Confirm first that the CI Go test jobs build with cgo enabled.
6. Delete the two Solidity fuzzers, the `cgo_test` tag and the `just fuzz-op-core-fees` recipe.

Both functions are small and frozen, so exploration adds little once each branch has a pinned vector, and the question of a scheduled fuzz job goes away.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.2*

topIssues.title: op-reth: Carry --txpool.enforce-tracked-nonce from reth#28526
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
Carry [paradigmxyz/reth#28526](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28526) on the reth fork and repin the monorepo to the new tag, so op-reth can turn on `--txpool.enforce-tracked-nonce`. This follows the transaction-delay investigation behind ethereum-optimism/infrastructure-services#1767. That PR fixes the `already known` errors in proxyd through deployment config, and it treats the delayed inclusion as a separate txpool race on the sequencer.

## Background

- [paradigmxyz/reth#26980](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/26980): under sustained load, validation against a stale account snapshot can insert a transaction below the sender's tracked nonce as pending. The sender's later, valid transactions then stop being selected.
- [paradigmxyz/reth#26981](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/26981) (`75d5872086604ff3d84889ef3792df48e6955188`) adds the opt-in fix `PoolConfig::enforce_tracked_nonce`. It is **already in `op-v2.7.0-1`**, which develop pins today, but it is off by default and `TxPoolArgs::pool_config` hard-codes it. The only way to turn it on is to replace the pool builder.
- [paradigmxyz/reth#28526](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28526) (`3e88af42a04264f1ad32d1bde14f67025de152be`, merged 2026-11-13) adds the `--txpool.enforce-tracked-nonce` flag, off by default. No upstream release contains it yet.

op-reth builds its pool from `ctx.pool_config()` (`rust/op-reth/crates/node/src/node.rs`), so the flag reaches the OP pool with no op-reth code change.

## Tasks

### Fork (`ethereum-optimism/reth`)

- [ ] Cherry-pick `3e88af42a04264f1ad32d1bde14f67025de152be` with `-x` onto `op-v2.7.0`. Its tip is `op-v2.7.0-1` (`ed91041f36b973eda3521ff90b3a25165087c133`). A dry-run merge applies cleanly; it touches `crates/node/core/src/args/txpool.rs` and `docs/vocs/docs/pages/cli/reth/node.mdx`.
- [ ] Open a fork PR, then merge it once `reth-act` passes.
- [ ] Tag `op-v2.7.0-2` on the merge commit.

### Monorepo

- [ ] Repin `rust/Cargo.toml` from `op-v2.7.0-1` to `op-v2.7.0-2`, and update the `op-v2.7.0-1` references in op-reth source comments (follow the `update-reth` skill).
- [ ] Regenerate the op-reth CLI snapshot (`rust/op-reth/crates/cli/tests/snapshots/cli.snap`) for the new flag.
- [ ] Add a test showing that `--txpool.enforce-tracked-nonce` reaches op-reth's final pool config, including through `pool_config_overrides`.

### Downstream

- [ ] Repin optimism-premium to the monorepo merge commit and the new reth tag.
- [ ] Release op-reth with the new pin.

### Rollout (out of scope for the code change, tracked here)

- [ ] Decide with infra which nodes enable `--txpool.enforce-tracked-nonce`. Upstream recommends it mainly for chains without reorgs and with very short block times: a reorg can leave the tracked sender state older than the validation snapshot. The sequencer is the main candidate. Check what this means for replicas, and for the sequencer after an unsafe reorg.

topPRs.title: docs: add ZK proofs documentation
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
Adds public docs for the ZK proof system, which is replacing Cannon-based fault proofs, so operators and readers have docs before ZK proofs ship.

- New "ZK Proofs" section under How the protocol works: hub, explainer, ZK dispute game, proof system, components, security, and reference.
- Operator pages: configuring op-zk-proposer and op-challenger for ZK games, verifying a ZK absolute prestate, and migrating a chain to ZK proofs via `opcm.upgrade`.
- An op-zk-proposer component page, a ZK section in the op-dispute-mon monitoring docs, and a shared "experimental" warning snippet.

Open items, marked as TODO comments in the pages:

- Standard values for `maxChallengeDuration`, `maxProveDuration`, `challengerBond`, and the init bond.
- The op-contracts release and superchain-ops template that support the ZK game.
- The op-zk-proposer image name and tag format.
- Adding op-zk-proposer to the component reference and release notes generators.
- Local prover support. The proposer currently proves only through the Succinct Prover Network.

The spec's `ZKDisputeGameConfig` includes a `verifier` field, but the OPCM struct doesn't: OPCM supplies its own `SP1PlonkAdapter`. These docs follow the code.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/3

topPRs.title: op-reth!: drop the generics that only ever take one type
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
op-reth's crates carried type parameters that every caller, in this repo and in optimism-premium, fills with the same type. They make every bound and signature longer, suggest extension points no one uses, and stand in the way of the next step: turning op-reth into one concrete node with a small, tempo-style overrides API that optimism-premium can wrap instead of re-implementing op-reth's node and launch code.

This PR removes them in three commits, meant to be reviewed one at a time:

1. **EVM and payload stack** (`db294887a1`). `OpEvmConfig`, `OpBlockAssembler`, the payload builder and payload types, and the debug witness RPCs lose their chain spec, node primitives, receipt builder and payload-attributes parameters.
2. **Node, RPC, engine and consensus wiring** (`fbe3502e19`). `OpAddOns` becomes `OpAddOns<N>`; `OpEngineTypes`, `OpEngineValidator`, `OpEngineApi`, `OpBeaconConsensus`, `OpExecutionPayloadValidator` and `OpSdmAdminApi` lose their single-instantiation parameters; `OpFullNodeTypes` folds into `OpNodeTypes`.
3. **Payload transactions, txpool, storage and CLI** (`2bf0e403ab`). `OpPayloadBuilder`'s `Txs` hook and the `OpPayloadTransactions` trait go; `OpPooledTransaction` and `OpStorage` become concrete; `OpCustomTransactionPool` drops its blob-store parameter; `Cli`, `Commands`, `CliApp`, `InitStateCommandOp` and the `proofs` subcommands drop their chain spec parser and RPC validator parameters.

No effect on operators or chains: no RPC method, wire format, metric, flag or config key changes, and block building, execution and validation run the same code. Only the Rust API changes.

A few changes go slightly past removing parameters, because removing them made something else dead:
- `OpEngineTypes` moves into the payload crate and replaces `OpPayloadTypes`, which had an identical `PayloadTypes` impl. The RPC crate's `OpEngineApi` needs to name it, and the RPC crate cannot depend on the node crate.
- `OpEngineValidator` loses its provider, which only the hand-written `Clone` read.
- `OpAddOns::min_suggested_priority_fee` goes; the value still reaches the eth API through `OpEthApiBuilder`.
- The `engine-api-access` example goes: it only showed replacing the engine API builder, which `OpAddOns` no longer allows.
- The `priority` node test goes: it only exercised the removed payload-transactions hook.

Kept generic on purpose, because optimism-premium or op-reth-test-engine fills them with their own types: `OpEvmConfig`'s `EvmFactory`; `OpPayloadBuilder`'s `Pool`/`Client`/`Evm`; `OpPayloadBuilderCtx`'s `Evm`; `OpPoolBuilder`'s transaction type, ordering and validator wrapper; `DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder`'s service; `OpEthApi`'s node; `Cli`'s extension args; and the engine type on the `OpEngineApi` RPC trait (premium's in-process tests call `OpEngineApiClient::<OpEngineTypes>`). `OpEngineApi` keeps its `Validator` parameter because the validator type lives in the node crate, which the RPC crate cannot name.

optimism-premium compiles against this branch in ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#493: its fallout is type-argument edits and one alias (`PremiumCli = Cli<PremiumCliArgs>`).

Reviews: rust-code-reviewer and deletion-reviewer ran on each commit. They found no behavior change. Applied: their leftover-docs and orphaned-dependency findings, and making the `proofs` subcommands concrete. Not taken: dropping the txpool transaction type parameters (premium's policy pool uses its own type), dropping the engine type from the `OpEngineApi` RPC trait (premium's tests use it), and a type alias for `OpEthApiBuilder`'s `EthApi`.

BREAKING CHANGE: Rust crates that build on op-reth must drop the removed type arguments and items:
- `OpEvmConfig<ChainSpec, N, R, EvmFactory>` is now `OpEvmConfig<EvmFactory>`, built for `OpChainSpec`, `OpPrimitives` and `OpRethReceiptBuilder`. `OpEvmConfig::new` is removed (use `OpEvmConfig::optimism`), and `new_with_evm_factory` no longer takes a receipt builder. Bound an EVM config by `NextBlockEnvCtx = OpNextBlockEnvAttributes` instead of `BuildNextEnv<...>`.
- `OpBlockAssembler`, `OpPayloadBuilderAttributes`, `OpBuiltPayload` and the `Attrs` parameter of `OpPayloadBuilderCtx`, `OpPayloadBuilder`, `OpDebugWitnessApi` and `DebugApiExt` are gone, as are the `OpPayloadPrimitives`, `OpAttributes` and `OpReplayNodePrimitives` traits and the unused `ExecutedPayload`. Read `OpPayloadBuilderAttributes`' public fields instead of the `OpAttributes` methods.
- `OpPayloadTypes` becomes `OpEngineTypes` (now in `reth-optimism-payload-builder`, still re-exported from `reth-optimism-node`), `OpFullNodeTypes` becomes `OpNodeTypes`, and `OpEngineValidator::new` takes only the chain spec. `OpAddOns::{with_engine_api, with_payload_validator, with_engine_validator, with_rpc_middleware}` and `OpAddOnsBuilder::with_rpc_middleware` are gone; a node that needs a different engine API or validator implements its own add-ons.
- `OpPayloadBuilder::with_transactions` and `OpPayloadTransactions` are gone: the payload builder always takes the pool's best transactions. `OpPooledTransaction` takes no type arguments, the unused `OpTransactionPool` alias is gone, `OpCustomTransactionPool<S, V, O>` is `OpCustomTransactionPool<V, O>`, and `OpPoolBuilder` only builds pools for nodes whose types are `OpNodeTypes`.
- `Cli<OpChainSpecParser, Args>` becomes `Cli<Args>`; `Commands`, `CliApp`, `InitStateCommandOp` and the `proofs` subcommands take no chain spec parser.

topPRs.title: op-service,op-node: return errors instead of panicking on malformed RPC responses
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
A broken or malicious RPC endpoint could crash op-node, op-batcher, op-proposer, op-challenger, op-conductor or op-supernode by answering with JSON `null` or by omitting a field the caller dereferences. The clients now check these responses where they enter and return an error. Nothing changes for a well-formed response.

Now an error instead of a panic:

- `RollupClient` (`outputAtBlock`, `safeHeadAtL1Block`, `syncStatus`, `rollupConfig`, `dependencySet`) and `OPStackClient.SealBlock`: a `null` result.
- `EngineAPIClient.GetPayload` and `OPStackClient.SealBlock`: an envelope without an execution payload. In op-node's sealing this is the existing retryable seal error.
- `SuperNodeClient.SuperRootAtTimestamp`: super root data without `super`, or an optimistic entry without its output.
- Receipts validation: a `null` log.
- `AccountResult.Verify`: a missing balance.
- `L2Client` output roots: an Isthmus header without a withdrawals root.
- txmgr's receipt query: a receipt or tip block number that is missing or doesn't fit in a uint64. It is handled like a failed RPC call and retried. A missing tip base fee is no longer passed to the metric.
- `L1InfoDeposit`: an L1 block without a base fee. No supported L1 has such a block, so derivation of valid L1 data is unchanged. The error is critical, like the other L1 info deposit errors. kona treats such a block's base fee as 0; that difference predates this change, which only replaces a panic.

Also: `CachingReceiptsProvider` releases its per-block lock when a fetch fails.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2*

topPRs.title: ci: gate proposal/** branches with a ci-gate-proposals workflow
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
Me: Define a subset of CI workflows that are required on proposal branches. Since  only op-contracts and op-deployer are released from those branches, we only care about workflows affecting them.

Claude: 

Release branches (`proposal/**`) run the full develop CI and rot within weeks of being cut: Rust toolchain drift, new RUSTSEC advisories and a Codecov uploader that none of the branch's own changes touch. A patch release then starts with days of unrelated fix-ups, which is why we did not ship an `op-deployer/0.7.x` patch in August. Context and plan: [P/PS: Release Branch CI Maintainability](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/P-PS-Release-Branch-CI-Maintainability-3c6f153ee16280958a4fcb71400aa658).

After this change, a proposal branch, a PR into it, its merge queue and an API trigger on it run one workflow, `release-branch`, and are gated by its one check, `ci-gate-proposals`: the contracts jobs that `required-contracts-ci` gates on develop, the NUT and op-deployer forge-version checks, and `go-tests`. Nothing changes for `develop` or feature PRs into it. A PR is routed by its base, so a PR from a proposal branch into develop still gets the develop gates.

Two things a reviewer cannot see in the diff:

- **The proposal/\*\* GitHub ruleset must require `ci-gate-proposals` before this config reaches a release branch.** On a proposal branch none of the four develop gates are produced, so a ruleset that still requires them blocks every PR rather than passing it unverified. Today `enforce-ci-checks-develop` covers `proposal/op-contracts/v7.*` and `v8.*`. This PR only lands the config on `develop`; the ruleset change and the cherry-pick onto v8.0.0 and v9.0.0 are separate steps.
- **A branch pushed before its PR exists is routed as a develop PR**, since there is no base yet. A push after the PR is opened re-routes it. The usual `git push` then `gh pr create` flow against a release branch therefore needs one more push.

Dismissed from the CI config review: keeping the whole `go-tests` job rather than splitting op-deployer's tests out. We want to see whether the Go suite rots on a release branch before paying for a split.

A PR into `develop` never takes the new routing, so this PR's own checks do not exercise the workflow. The same commits are pushed to a throwaway [`proposal/ci-test`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/proposal/ci-test) branch, where the routing takes the release-branch path and `ci-gate-proposals` is the only gate: [CI runs on that branch](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism?branch=proposal%2Fci-test). The runs at [f1d8917](https://app.circleci.com/workflow/636ff79d-a051-48b0-90e4-ece304c1d92c), [897f167](https://app.circleci.com/workflow/205a6488-9419-4009-8edc-629c44b89f80) and [4db2ed9](https://app.circleci.com/workflow/d7da5e50-de1a-4951-b2bc-91696d33683a) (the current head) all passed.

topPRs.title: docs: add Upgrade 22 (Lagoon) notice and archive completed notices
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
## Summary

New provisional notice page for **Upgrade 22 (Lagoon)** at `docs/public-docs/notices/upgrade-22.mdx`, plus a nav entry in `docs.json`, a card on `notices/index.mdx`, and matching updates to the interop-prep notice and the Lagoon hardfork page. It also archives the Upgrade 21, Subblocks, and preconfirmation architecture notices. Target: live Fri Nov 20.

- **Audience:** users, app developers and integrators, node operators, chain operators (including permissionless fault-proof chains).
- **Covers:** Lagoon scope and chains (OP Mainnet + Unichain interop, Ink and Soneium without interop), the `OPContractsManagerV2.migrate` shared dispute contracts, withdrawal re-proving, message expiry, the L2 ETH bridge pause, post-exec transactions / SDM (Unichain as the first adopter), BLS12-381 limits, permissionless prestate steps, and the timing table with the registry activation timestamps.
- **Form:** notice, modeled on `notices/upgrade-21.mdx` and the permissionless section of the Upgrade 18 archive. It links to `notices/interop-prep` for the supernode topology and does not repeat it.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/public-docs/notices/upgrade-22.mdx` | New page |
| `docs/public-docs/docs.json` | Adds `notices/upgrade-22` to Network Upgrades |
| `docs/public-docs/notices/index.mdx` | Adds the Upgrade 22 card (Lagoon, interop, shared dispute contracts, re-proving, SDM, ZK dispute game); removes the archived cards |
| `notices/{upgrade-21,subblocks,preconfirmation-architecture-transition}.mdx` → `notices/archive/` | Archived per the index RETENTION rule: redirects in `docs.json`, rows in `notices/archive/index.mdx`, `date:` frontmatter, `nav-allowlist.json` entries, Upgrade 21 row in the contract upgrades table, inbound English links repointed. `ko/` is left to the translation sync, as with the Upgrade 20 archive. |
| `docs/public-docs/snippets/zk-proofs-status.mdx` | Softens the ZK status callout on the ZK proofs pages: ready for production chains with Upgrade 22 |
| `docs/public-docs/notices/interop-prep.mdx` | Replaces "timestamps not yet set" with the registry values, notes Ink and Soneium activate Lagoon without interop, links the Upgrade 22 notice |
| `docs/public-docs/op-stack/protocol/hardforks/lagoon.mdx` (+ regenerated snippet) | Points the registry entry at the Upgrade 22 notice, adds the per-chain activation table, refreshes scope from the current spec overview |

## What to review

**Needs a feature engineer:**

1. Withdrawal re-proving after `migrate` (`OptimismPortal2.sol` checkWithdrawal/isGameClaimValid against the shared ASR; maturity delay restarts from the new proof).
2. Permissionless section: `OP_PROPOSER_GAME_TYPE` stays `9` through the hardfork, the interop prestate is set onchain by the governed migration, and third-party challengers move to the shared factory.
3. Component tables: all versions are "To be published" until the Lagoon releases exist. Node operators: op-node, op-reth, op-supernode (kona-node dropped, not production-ready). Chain operators: op-batcher, op-challenger, op-dispute-mon, op-zk-proposer. op-challenger v1.12.0 and op-dispute-mon v1.6.6 already contain ZK game support; confirm whether new releases are needed for the ZK switch.

**Open (rendered as "to be published", tracked as MDX TODO comments):**

- Node versions, Lagoon `kona-client`/`kona-host` tag, prestate hashes, `op-challenger` version.
- The `op-challenger` version with the `zk` game type. (ZK switch dates are now in: Sepolia 2026-12-11, Mainnet 2027-01-14.) Pre-switch proofs stay valid (checked against `AnchorStateRegistry`), and the section links the ZK docs merged in #23751.
- Whether Ink and Soneium get an L1 contract upgrade in U22.
- L1StandardBridge-target rejection: `v10.0.0-rc.1` rejects unconditionally, #24011 on develop narrows it; omitted until the final tag.

**Judgment calls:**

- Activation timestamps are included from superchain-registry `main` (already merged) rather than left blank.

## Test plan

- [x] `lint_draft.py` clean; `check_snippets.py` 2/2 pass; `docs.json` parses.
- [x] Adversarial verifier pass: 41 claims re-derived from source; review-law 24 pass / 0 fail.
- [x] `mint dev` renders the notice, interop-prep, and Lagoon pages and the sidebar; no TODO text renders.
- [ ] Solutions DRI and at least one feature engineer approve the complete page.
